claim: The natural numbers can be axiomatized (Peano axioms) providing a consistent foundation for arithmetic

evidence.title: Dedekind's Contributions to the Foundations of Mathematics (SEP)
evidence.finding: Peano's axioms, building on Dedekind's work, provide the standard axiomatization of natural numbers used in mathematics

evidence.title: Philosophy of Mathematics (SEP)
evidence.finding: The Peano axioms are accepted as the foundation for arithmetic across all major schools of mathematical philosophy

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Axioms are stipulated, not empirically discovered — they define the system rather than describe observations
scoreReasoning.coherence: Internally consistent (assuming consistency of PA, which is provable from stronger systems) and foundational to all arithmetic
scoreReasoning.convergence: Near-universal acceptance in mathematics; debates are about foundations (set theory vs category theory) not about PA itself
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: All computation, computer science, and applied mathematics depend on arithmetic grounded in these axioms

claim: ZFC set theory provides a consistent axiomatic foundation for most of mathematics

evidence.title: Set Theory (SEP)
evidence.finding: ZFC is the standard axiomatic framework for mathematics, though its consistency cannot be proved within the system itself

evidence.title: Axiom of Choice (SEP)
evidence.finding: The axiom of choice, included in ZFC, is independent of the other axioms and enables important but counterintuitive results

scoreReasoning.correspondence: ZFC axioms are formal postulates, not empirical claims — consistency is assumed rather than proved
scoreReasoning.coherence: Provides a unified foundation for analysis, algebra, topology, and most mathematical disciplines
scoreReasoning.convergence: Dominant foundational system; alternatives (category theory, type theory) exist but ZFC remains standard
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: Virtually all modern mathematics can be formalized in ZFC; essential infrastructure for mathematical practice

claim: A formal proof guarantees truth-preservation from axioms to theorems within the system

evidence.title: Proof Theory (SEP)
evidence.finding: Proof theory studies the structure of formal proofs and establishes that valid inference rules preserve truth

evidence.title: Kurt Goedel (SEP)
evidence.finding: Goedel's completeness theorem (1930) shows that first-order logic is complete: every valid formula has a formal proof

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Proof validity is a formal/syntactic property — it is verified by checking steps, not by empirical observation
scoreReasoning.coherence: Central to all of mathematics; the completeness theorem provides strong theoretical backing
scoreReasoning.convergence: Universal agreement in mathematics and logic about the validity of formal proof
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: Computer-verified proofs, cryptography, and formal verification in software all depend on proof validity

claim: Any consistent formal system powerful enough to encode arithmetic is incomplete — there exist true statements it cannot prove (Goedel)

evidence.title: Goedel's Incompleteness Theorems (SEP)
evidence.finding: Goedel proved in 1931 that any consistent formal system capable of expressing arithmetic contains undecidable propositions

evidence.title: On Formally Undecidable Propositions (Goedel 1931)
evidence.finding: The original proof constructing a self-referential sentence that is true but unprovable within the system

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Goedel's proof is a rigorous mathematical result — it is verified, not empirical, but the correspondence is to mathematical truth
scoreReasoning.coherence: Consistent with and complementary to proof theory; constrains but does not undermine formal reasoning
scoreReasoning.convergence: Universally accepted in mathematics and logic; no serious challenge to the theorem exists
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: Constrains expectations about what formal systems can achieve; important for computer science (halting problem)

claim: Mathematics can model physical systems with predictive accuracy far exceeding chance

evidence.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Mathematics in the Natural Sciences (Wigner 1960)
evidence.finding: Wigner observed that mathematical formulations yield astonishingly accurate predictions about physical phenomena, a fact he considered mysterious

evidence.title: Mathematical Explanation (SEP)
evidence.finding: Mathematics plays an indispensable explanatory role in physics, suggesting deep structural connections between math and physical reality

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Mathematical models make precise, quantitative predictions that are directly testable — GPS, particle physics, orbital mechanics all confirm this
scoreReasoning.coherence: Consistent with the view that the universe has mathematical structure; the applicability of math to physics is well-documented
scoreReasoning.convergence: Universal agreement that math is effective in physics; debate about why (structural realism vs instrumentalism)
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: Engineering, technology, and modern physics are entirely built on mathematical models with extraordinary predictive success

claim: Mathematical reasoning provides a consistent, formal framework for deriving necessary truths from axioms, applicable to modeling physical reality

evidence.title: Philosophy of Mathematics (SEP)
evidence.finding: Mathematics occupies a unique epistemic position: its truths are necessary within axiom systems and remarkably applicable to physical reality

evidence.title: Platonism in the Philosophy of Mathematics (SEP)
evidence.finding: Whether mathematical objects exist independently (Platonism) or are human constructions remains debated, but mathematics' effectiveness is undisputed

scoreReasoning.correspondence: The overall claim combines formal and empirical elements — the formal part is verified internally, the applicability part is empirically supported
scoreReasoning.coherence: Integrates foundations, proof theory, incompleteness constraints, and empirical applicability into a coherent picture
scoreReasoning.convergence: Broad agreement on the power and applicability of mathematics; ongoing philosophical debates about its nature
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: Mathematics is the language of science, engineering, and technology — its practical value is beyond dispute
